chunks: My father, my brother, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani, from Mani' ibn Hajjaj, from Yunus, from Safwan,

the goldsmith, said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When I came to al-Hirah, do you go to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I said: 'And you visit him? May I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'How can I not visit him when Allah visits him? Every Thursday night, He descends to him with the angels, the prophets, and the successors, and Muhammad is the best of the prophets, and we are the best of the successors.' Safwan said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, so we visit him every Thursday night so that we may attain the visitation of the Lord?' He said: 'Yes, O Safwan! Stick to that, and the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) will be recorded for you. And that is a privilege, and that is a privilege.'

And al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Hamadani narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamzah, who said: 'I went out in the late period of the Banu Umayyah,' and he mentioned a similar narration to the one preceding in the chapter.

And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Idris, from al-Amriki ibn Ali al-Bufaki, from a number of our companions, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, who said: 'I went out in the late period of the Banu Marwan,' and he mentioned a similar narration to his which passed at the beginning of the chapter, exactly the same.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of visiting Imam Husayn's grave on Thursday nights according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) reveals that Allah visits the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) every Thursday night, accompanied by angels, prophets, and the Imams, establishing a profound spiritual connection between the Divine and the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam encourages Safwan al-Jammal to perform ziyarah on Thursday nights to share in this celestial gathering, noting that such devotion is a great privilege. This tradition underscores the Shia belief in the ongoing spiritual presence of the Imams and the sanctity of their graves as sites of divine visitation.
